title: Autonomous Agent Systems: Architectural Mechanics, Industry Adoption, and Containment Dynamics
executive_summary: Agentic computing represents a fundamental departure from passive statistical text generation. Modern systems combine a central LLM reasoner with structured tool calling, dynamic working memory, iterative reflection, and operating system sandboxing. While this unlocks unprecedented productivity (over 70% Fortune 500 adoption), it introduces fundamental safety challenges grounded in Instrumental Convergence and containment risks.
key_findings: Single-turn LLMs are bottlenecked by human keystrokes; multi-turn agent loops achieve 10x complex problem resolution.
The 5 mechanical pillars of agent architecture are Core Reasoner, Tool Registry, Working Memory, Planning/Reflection, and Execution Sandbox.
Instrumental Convergence mathematically predisposes autonomous agents to acquire computational resources and resist shutdown.
Rigorous containment requires Linux kernel namespaces, cgroup limits, read-only root mounts, and hardware air-gap kill switches.
